source_text: ηβον εἶναι γένος, καὶ χαλινῶν τῶν εἰς ἐγκράτειαν οὐ λίαν ἀνέχεται. Ἀλλ' ἦν ἀκλόνητος ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἰωσὴφ, οὐ τὸ τῆς νεότητος ἀνειμένον ἀπαιδαγώγητον ἔχων, οὐ δεδιὼς ὅτι ξένος ἦν καὶ οἰκέτης. Ἐκβεβίαστο γὰρ εἰς ἄμφω παρὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν τοῖς Ἰσμαηλίταις καταπωλούμενος. Ἐπεὶ δὲ κρείττων ἦν ἡδονῆς τε ἅμα τῆς μυσαρωτάτης, καὶ τῶν εἰς ἀσέλγειαν κινημάτων, συκοφαντεῖ τὸ γύναιον, καὶ ἀντίστροφον τῷ νέῳ ποιεῖται τὴν γραφήν. Τὸν δὲ, οὐκ εἴκοντα τοῖς αὐτῆς αἰτήμασιν, ὑβριστὴν ἀπεκάλει. Καὶ δεσμώτης μὲν ἐντεῦθεν ὁ νεανίας ἦν· θείᾳ
pass_a_gloss: §32 dual gloss: ἰσοπαλής / equal · φιλοθεέω / God-love · ἐγκράτεια / continence … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Equal wage from God; approach churches washed—Book 14 ends.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ...equal the wage from the prize-giver God. So then the young race is somehow unbridled, and does not very much bear the bridles unto continence. But unshaken was the all-divine Joseph, not having the relaxed of youth unpedagogued, not fearing that he was a stranger and house-servant. For he had been forced unto both by the brothers, being sold-down to the Ishmaelites. And since he was stronger than both pleasure the most polluted, and the movements unto wantonness, the little-woman slanders, and makes reverse for the youth the writing. And him, not yielding to her asks, she was calling insolent. And a bound one thereafter the youth was; yet by divine grace he was being saved, and a wage of continence he gained-out at once, the ruling all the land of the Egyptians. So then even if the matter should have labors, even if heavy sweats should lie-before of the boasts unto continence, not great is the word, for the one having altogether chosen to God-love; for he will have, he will have also equal the from God. Therefore those wishing to frequent the churches must approach washed from sin's stain—clean in manners as the law's clean creatures, continent as Joseph—so as to stand beside God in spirit and truth.
